newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares soar on rate cut, upbeat bank results.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares soar on rate cut, upbeat bank results.

text.p: Greek shares shot ahead in early Friday trading on the back of Thursday's 1.68 percent leap on news of strong half-year banking profits and a cut in the central bank's depo rates.
"A widespread mood of optimism was evident from Thursday's session ahead of the announcement of superb half-year performance by core banking stocks," said Paul Vranas, broker at Euroxx Securities.
"The results vindicated earlier forecasts, raising hopes for upbeat performance for the entire banking sector in 1997."
National Bank and Alpha Credit Bank turned in large profit growth in their interim results announced late on Thursday.

"Helped by low supply, core banking stocks add to their value because investors had stayed on the sidelines and prices had not fully incorporated those expectations," he said. "This could be the start to something bigger in the medium-term, especially if buying interest filters through to a wider range of industrials and medium-caps."
Sentiment has also been boosted by the central bank's rate cut which led to lower interest rates and government paper yields, he said.

Effective today, the Bank of Greece cut its basic and floor deposit facility rates by 30 basis points. It cited a large drop in interbank surplus liquidity and wider spreads between drachma and other EMS currency rates.
Depo rates and treasury yields were sharply lower after the late Thursday announcement.

The Athens general index was up 1.47 percent or 23.06 points at 1,592.21 from Thursday's close of 1,569.15 after 15 minutes of trading, with banks and industrials gaining 2.23 and 1.24 percent respectively.
Turnover was 1.9 billion drachmas on volume of 0.34 million shares.
Advancers led decliners 86 to 20 with 20 shares unchanged on 126 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $10.6-$10.85. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,122-1,152 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,100-1,160 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock were unchanged at 6,380 drachmas.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 619.73-659.29 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $68.35-$71.08. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,385-3,605 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $11.17 bid/no offer. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 227-259 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
